title: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle: one job, four vocabularies

videos.script: Four engines run most of the relational data in the world. PostgreSQL, MySQL, Microsoft's SQL Server and Oracle. {{four}} From a distance they look like four different trades. Different installers, different tools, different words for everything. {{words}} Up close, every one of them is the same machine. A process that owns a directory of files. A cache of those files in memory. A log where every change is written before the data itself. And a list of who may do what. {{machine}} So a DBA who understands one of them already understands most of the others. What changes is the vocabulary. {{vocabulary}} And the vocabulary is a trap. In MySQL a database is what everybody else calls a schema. In Oracle a schema is a user. In SQL Server a login and a user are two different things. {{trap}} This lesson lays the four side by side, so that the rest of the course can speak PostgreSQL without leaving you stranded on the day the server in front of you is one of the others. {{title}}
